newsitem.title: MEXICO: RESEARCH ALERT - GCC raised to buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - GCC raised to buy.

text.p: Robert Fleming Inc said Monday it upgraded Mexican cement maker Grupo Cementos de Chihuahua (GCC) to buy from long term buy.
Analyst Ben Unglow said attractive valuations were behind the upgrade despite the company's "somewhat weaker than expected" Q1 earnings, which were hurt by cost increases.

Unglow said anti-dumping tariffs imposed by the United States on Mexican cement "should be considered as an ongoing cost of the business; however, the 28.2 percent decrease in the stock price since its high point on Sept 24, 1996, accommodates the new outlook."
"Cost increases are not expected to impact results throughout the year, and margins are expected to recover from Q1 1997 levels," he added.

"Although the concern over lack of earnings momentum remains, the valuation argument is now extremely compelling. The sharp drop in the stock price is considered a buying opportunity and it is believed that GCC can continue to grow its business successfully as Mexican demand recovers despite thr rise in duties," he said.
